critical_code_review_comments: storage.py upload_logo: extension check is filename-based only — a user could upload arbitrary binary named 'foo.png'. Content-type sniffing (e.g., magic bytes) would be safer against MIME confusion but low-risk given tenant-only auth.

storage.py remove_logo iterates all pages and unconditionally $sets blocks even when no navbar/footer existed — harmless but generates unnecessary writes. Also does not return pages_updated count for consistency with upload_logo.

server.py build_export_files line 646: `ext = logo.rsplit('.', 1)[-1] if '.' in logo else 'png'` assumes the URL always has a valid extension — safe today because upload enforces it, but downstream _rewrite() replaces the exact url string only; if the same logo URL happened to be substring of another (unlikely), silent double-replace could occur.
LogoUpload.jsx: onChange(data.logo) followed by parent load() double-fetches; small perf nit, not a bug.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (upload → toast → navbar/footer/current → remove → re-upload → public preview all pass)
